icp_fit_score_v1.title: ICP fit score
icp_fit_score_v1.use: AI column that scores accounts or contacts against workspace ICP context.
icp_fit_score_v1.prompt: Score this account/contact against the ICP context. Use only the provided row fields and context. Return JSON with fit_label, fit_score from 0 to 100, rationale, matched_signals, disqualifiers, and next_action.

account_research_summary_v1.title: Account research summary
account_research_summary_v1.use: AI column that compresses raw company research into usable GTM notes.
account_research_summary_v1.prompt: Summarize the company for a GTM operator. Include what they sell, likely buyer, current signals, why now, and risks. Do not invent facts. Return concise JSON.

personalization_fact_v1.title: Personalization fact
personalization_fact_v1.use: AI column for one evidence-backed personalization point.
personalization_fact_v1.input_kind_rejection_hint: Map at least one column produced by research, enrichment, or a tool. Mapping only manual name/title/company columns produces template output. See enriching-and-researching.md.
personalization_fact_v1.prompt: Find one specific, relevant, non-generic personalization fact from the provided row evidence. Return JSON with fact, source_field, confidence, and why_it_matters.

person_role_summary_v1.title: Person role summary
person_role_summary_v1.use: AI column that turns a LinkedIn headline and bio into one plain sentence about what a person actually does.
person_role_summary_v1.input_kind_rejection_hint: A role summary must read scraped or enriched evidence. Mapping only manual name/title/company columns just restates the title. Map the headline, bio, or another enrichment column first. See enriching-and-researching.md.
person_role_summary_v1.prompt: Describe what this person does professionally, in ONE plain sentence of at most 180 characters, using only the provided row evidence. Say what they do, at what kind of company (the category, not its name), and who they do it for. Write it as a colleague would describe them to someone else: no emoji, no pipe separators, no slogans or taglines, no first person, no marketing voice, and never the headline copied back verbatim. Do not invent facts. If the evidence is too thin to describe the role honestly, return description null — do not return the word unknown or any other placeholder text.

email_draft_v1.title: Outbound email draft
email_draft_v1.use: AI column for a short first-touch email draft.
email_draft_v1.input_kind_rejection_hint: Outbound copy must reference research or enrichment for at least one mapped input column. Map a column from research, enrichment, or a tool before adding this draft column. See enriching-and-researching.md.
email_draft_v1.prompt: Write a concise first-touch B2B outbound email using only the provided evidence and positioning. Avoid hype, unsupported claims, and fake familiarity. The subject and body must reference something specific to the row that did not come from name, title, or company alone. Populate evidence_used with the names of the mapped input columns you actually drew from. Set requires_human_review to true when evidence is thin, claims are weak, or any disqualifier is plausible. Return JSON with subject, body, personalization_source, evidence_used, requires_human_review, and risk_notes.

qualification_qa_v1.title: Qualification QA
qualification_qa_v1.use: AI column that audits whether a row is ready for outbound or sync.
qualification_qa_v1.prompt: Audit this row for outbound readiness. Check missing fields, weak evidence, disqualifiers, unsupported claims, and sync blockers. Return JSON with status, blockers, warnings, and recommended_next_step.

signal_extraction_v1.title: Signal extraction
signal_extraction_v1.use: AI column that extracts buying signals from raw text or provider payloads.
signal_extraction_v1.prompt: Extract concrete buying signals from the provided text or JSON. Group by hiring, funding, product, tech stack, compliance, expansion, and pain. Return only signals supported by evidence.

sequence_outline_v1.title: Outbound sequence outline
sequence_outline_v1.use: AI column or planning prompt for a fixed-length multi-step outbound sequence.
sequence_outline_v1.input_kind_rejection_hint: Multi-step outbound copy must condition on at least one research or enrichment column. Map a column from research, enrichment, or a tool before adding this sequence column. See enriching-and-researching.md.
sequence_outline_v1.prompt: Design a 4-step outbound sequence for this row. Each step must reference a different angle (hook, proof, low-friction CTA, breakup) and condition on the mapped research or enrichment columns. Keep each body under 90 words. Populate personalization_source and evidence_used per step with the input column names actually referenced. Return JSON matching the output schema.

subject_line_variants_v1.title: Subject line variants
subject_line_variants_v1.use: AI column that produces multiple subject line variants for an existing draft or sequence step.
subject_line_variants_v1.input_kind_rejection_hint: Variants must condition on the draft or research column they are testing against. Map the source draft column or the research column before adding this variant column.
subject_line_variants_v1.prompt: Generate subject line variants for the provided draft or research evidence. Each subject must be at most seven words, must avoid clickbait, ALL CAPS, and exclamation marks, and must tie back to a concrete signal from the evidence. Return JSON matching the output schema with one entry per variant, including angle and a short rationale.

email_qa_critique_v1.title: Outbound copy QA critique
email_qa_critique_v1.use: AI column that audits an existing draft or sequence column for weak personalization, unsupported claims, and length issues, then proposes a tightened revision.
email_qa_critique_v1.input_kind_rejection_hint: The QA critique must read the draft or sequence column it is auditing. Map the source draft or sequence column before adding this critique column.
email_qa_critique_v1.prompt: Audit the provided outbound draft against the row's research and ICP evidence. Flag weak personalization, unsupported claims, length violations, off-tone copy, and any compliance issues. If the draft needs tightening, produce revised_subject and revised_body that keep the original structure and tighten only where evidence supports it. Return JSON matching the output schema.

crm_sync_review_v1.title: CRM sync review
crm_sync_review_v1.use: AI column or QA pass before external CRM/outbound writes.
crm_sync_review_v1.prompt: Review this row before external sync. Identify missing required fields, duplicate risks, provider ID conflicts, copy issues, and approval blockers. Return JSON.

clean_company_name_v1.title: Clean company name
clean_company_name_v1.use: The company name without Inc/LLC-style suffixes, punctuation or shouting caps, read from the company name column.

company.description: The column holding the company name as imported.

clean_job_title_v1.title: Clean job title
clean_job_title_v1.use: The job title without padding, hiring shout-outs or stray emoji, read from the job title column.

title.description: The column holding the job title as imported.

email_type_v1.title: Email type
email_type_v1.use: Whether an address is work, personal, role or disposable, read from the email column. When the built-in lists are not enough, the paid bounceban.check tool column adds live username and domain typing plus syntax validity for catch-all and SEG domains, at up to 1.7 credits an address.

email.description: The column holding the email address.

list_from_text_v1.title: Text to list
list_from_text_v1.use: A cell holding several values turned into a real list you can filter, count and feed into other columns, read from the text column.

text.description: The column holding several values in one cell, separated by commas, semicolons or pipes.

company_b2b_b2c_classification_v1.title: B2B or B2C
company_b2b_b2c_classification_v1.use: Whether a company sells to businesses, consumers or both, read from the company name, description and website columns.

company.description: A column holding the company name.

description.description: Company description, tagline or about text.

classification.description: Who the company sells to, or unknown when the fields do not say.

confidence.description: How sure the answer is, between 0 and 1.

reason.description: One sentence on why, from the provided fields.

evidence.description: The wording relied on, quoted from the provided fields, or null when none of them say.

company_b2b_b2c_classification_v1.prompt: Decide who {{company}} sells to. Use only the company name and, when the description or website inputs are provided, their text. Set classification to B2B when it sells to businesses, B2C when it sells to consumers, B2B_and_B2C when it clearly sells to both, and unknown when these fields do not say enough to tell — a familiar name is not evidence. Quote the wording you relied on in evidence, keep reason to one sentence, and set confidence between 0 and 1. Never add what the provided fields do not say. Return JSON matching the output schema.

pricing_plan_count_v1.title: Number of pricing plans
pricing_plan_count_v1.use: How many plans a pricing page lists, read from the pricing-page URL column.

plan_count.description: How many distinct plans the pricing page lists, or null when it lists none.

plan_names.description: The name of each plan, in the order the page shows them.

pricing_plan_count_v1.prompt: Read the pricing page and count the distinct plans it offers. Put that number in plan_count and every plan name, in the order shown, in plan_names. Do not count add-ons, credit packs, or monthly and yearly toggles as separate plans. If the page lists no plans, set plan_count to null and plan_names to an empty list.

pricing_range_v1.title: Pricing range
pricing_range_v1.use: Lowest and highest listed plan prices, read from the pricing-page URL column.

min_price.description: The lowest plan price stated on the page, as a plain number.

max_price.description: The highest plan price stated on the page, as a plain number.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for the currency the prices are quoted in.

billing_period.description: Billing period for the prices: month, year, one_time or unknown.

plans_priced.description: How many plans on the page show a price.

note.description: Short qualifier on the range, such as per-seat or usage-based pricing.

pricing_range_v1.prompt: Read the pricing page and find the lowest and highest plan prices it states. Put the plain numbers in min_price and max_price, the ISO currency code in currency, and month, year, one_time or unknown in billing_period. Set plans_priced to how many plans show a price, and use note for anything that qualifies the range, such as per-seat or usage-based pricing. If the page states no prices, set min_price, max_price, currency and note to null and plans_priced to 0.

pricing_top_plan_cost_v1.title: Most expensive plan cost
pricing_top_plan_cost_v1.use: Name and price of the top tier on a pricing page, read from the pricing-page URL column.

plan_name.description: Name of the most expensive plan, or null when the page names none.

price.description: Price of that plan as a plain number, or null when it is quote-only.

billing_period.description: Billing period for that price: month, year, one_time or unknown.

custom_quote.description: True when the top plan is quoted by sales rather than priced on the page.

pricing_top_plan_cost_v1.prompt: Read the pricing page and find its most expensive plan. Put its name in plan_name, its price as a plain number in price, the ISO currency code in currency, and month, year, one_time or unknown in billing_period. Set custom_quote to true when that plan is contact-sales or quote-only, and leave price null in that case. If the page shows no plans at all, set every other field to null and custom_quote to false.

pricing_top_plan_features_v1.title: Most expensive plan features
pricing_top_plan_features_v1.use: What the top tier includes, read from the pricing-page URL column.

plan_name.description: Name of the most expensive plan, or null when the page names none.

features.description: Each feature the page lists for that plan, in the page's own wording.

pricing_top_plan_features_v1.prompt: Read the pricing page and find its most expensive plan. Put that plan's name in plan_name and list what it includes in features, one short phrase per item, keeping the page's own wording. Include only the features shown for that plan, not the ones listed against lower tiers. If the page names no features for it, use an empty list.

pricing_enterprise_plan_v1.title: Enterprise or custom plan
pricing_enterprise_plan_v1.use: Whether a pricing page offers an enterprise or contact-sales tier, read from the pricing-page URL column.

has_enterprise_plan.description: True when the page offers an enterprise or custom tier.

plan_name.description: Name of that tier, or null when the page has none.

contact_sales.description: True when the tier asks the buyer to contact sales or request a quote.

stated_price.description: Price shown for that tier as a plain number, or null when none is shown.

pricing_enterprise_plan_v1.prompt: Read the pricing page and decide whether it offers an enterprise or custom tier. Set has_enterprise_plan accordingly and put that tier's name in plan_name. Set contact_sales to true when the tier asks the buyer to contact sales or request a quote, and put any number the page shows for it in stated_price. If there is no such tier, set has_enterprise_plan and contact_sales to false and the other fields to null.

pricing_plan_summary_v1.title: Pricing plan summary
pricing_plan_summary_v1.use: Plan count, cheapest (a free plan counts) and priciest tier, range and enterprise tier, from the pricing-page URL column.

plan_count.description: How many distinct plans the page lists, or null when it lists none.

name.description: Name of the plan, or null when the page names none.

price.description: Price of the plan as a plain number, or null when it is quote-only.

billing_period.description: Billing period for that price: month, year, one_time or unknown.

features.description: Each feature the page lists for that plan.

cheapest_plan.description: The lowest-priced plan on the page and what it includes. A free plan counts: its price is 0.

name.description: Name of the plan, or null when the page names none.

price.description: Price of the plan as a plain number, or null when it is quote-only.

billing_period.description: Billing period for that price: month, year, one_time or unknown.

features.description: Each feature the page lists for that plan.

most_expensive_plan.description: The highest-priced plan on the page and what it includes.

min_price.description: Lowest price stated anywhere on the page, as a plain number.

max_price.description: Highest price stated anywhere on the page, as a plain number.

price_range.description: The span between the lowest and highest prices the page states.

available.description: True when the page offers an enterprise or custom tier.

plan_name.description: Name of that tier, or null when the page has none.

contact_sales.description: True when that tier is quoted by sales rather than priced.

enterprise_plan.description: Whether the page offers an enterprise or custom tier, and how it is priced.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on how the plan lineup is structured.

pricing_plan_summary_v1.prompt: Read the pricing page and describe its whole plan lineup. Set plan_count, then fill cheapest_plan and most_expensive_plan with the plan name, the price as a plain number, the ISO currency code, the billing period (month, year, one_time or unknown) and the features listed for it. Fill price_range from the lowest and highest stated prices, and enterprise_plan from any custom or contact-sales tier. Write two or three sentences in summary on how the lineup is structured. Set anything the page does not state to null and use empty lists where it shows no features.

job_posting_summary_v1.title: Job posting summary
job_posting_summary_v1.use: Title, company, location and seniority of a role, read from the job-posting URL column.

title.description: The job title as written on the posting.

company.description: The hiring company named on the posting.

location.description: Where the role is based, including remote when the posting says so.

employment_type.description: Employment type such as full-time, part-time, contract or internship.

seniority.description: Seniority level such as junior, mid, senior, lead or executive.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on what the role actually does.

job_posting_summary_v1.prompt: Read the job posting and pull out its basics. Set title, company, location, employment_type and seniority from what the page states, not from what the role usually implies. Write summary as two or three sentences on what the person in this role would do. Set any field the page does not state to null.

job_posting_pay_range_v1.title: Job posting pay range
job_posting_pay_range_v1.use: Stated salary or hourly range on a job posting, read from the job-posting URL column.

min_pay.description: Bottom of the stated pay range, as a plain number.

max_pay.description: Top of the stated pay range, as a plain number.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for the pay figures.

pay_period.description: The period the pay figures cover.

stated.description: True only when the posting itself gives a pay number.

note.description: Short caveat such as equity, bonus or location-dependent pay.

job_posting_pay_range_v1.prompt: Read the job posting and find the pay it states. Put plain numbers in min_pay and max_pay, the ISO currency code in currency, and hour, month, year or unknown in pay_period. Set stated to true only when the posting itself gives a number, and use note for equity, bonus or location-dependent caveats. If no pay is stated, set stated to false and min_pay, max_pay and currency to null.

job_posting_requirements_v1.title: Key job requirements
job_posting_requirements_v1.use: Must-have and nice-to-have requirements on a job posting, read from the job-posting URL column.

nice_to_have.description: Each qualification the posting prefers but does not require.

years_experience.description: Lowest number of years of experience the posting asks for.

tools_and_skills.description: Each tool, platform, language or skill the posting names.

job_posting_requirements_v1.prompt: Read the job posting and separate what it demands from what it merely prefers. List required qualifications in must_have and preferred ones in nice_to_have, one short phrase each. Put the lowest number of years of experience the posting asks for in years_experience, and every named tool, platform or skill in tools_and_skills. Use empty lists and null where the page says nothing.

company_past_events_v1.title: Past company events
company_past_events_v1.use: Events, webinars and conferences a company has hosted, searched from the company name column.

company.description: The company name.

events.description: Each past event the evidence attributes to the company.

date.description: Date the event ran, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null when the evidence has none.

type.description: Kind of event, such as webinar, conference, meetup or summit.

url.description: Page for the event, or null when the evidence has none.

company_past_events_v1.prompt: Find events {{company}} has hosted, run or sponsored, such as conferences, webinars, meetups or user summits. Add one entry to events for each, with its name, its date as YYYY-MM-DD, its type, and its event page. Use only the evidence and skip events run by other companies. If the evidence shows none, use an empty list.

company_upcoming_event_v1.title: Upcoming company event
company_upcoming_event_v1.use: The next event a company is promoting, searched from the company name column.

company.description: The company name.

name.description: Name of the upcoming event, or null when the evidence names none.

date.description: Date the event starts, as YYYY-MM-DD.

type.description: Kind of event, such as webinar, conference, meetup or summit.

url.description: Registration or event page for it.

is_upcoming.description: True only when the evidence shows the event has not happened yet.

company_upcoming_event_v1.prompt: Find the next event {{company}} is promoting in the evidence. Fill name, date as YYYY-MM-DD, type, and url with the registration or event page. Set is_upcoming to true only when the evidence shows the event has not happened yet. If the evidence names no event, set the other fields to null and is_upcoming to false.

company_next_event_date_v1.title: Next event date
company_next_event_date_v1.use: The date of a company's next event, searched from the company name column.

company.description: The company name.

next_event_date.description: Date of the company's next event, as YYYY-MM-DD.

event_name.description: Name of that event, or null when the evidence names none.

url.description: Page for that event, or null when the evidence has none.

company_next_event_date_v1.prompt: Find the date of the next event {{company}} is running, using only the evidence. Put it in next_event_date as YYYY-MM-DD, the event's name in event_name, and its page in url. Prefer an exact date over a month or a season. If the evidence gives no date, set next_event_date to null and leave the other fields as whatever the evidence supports.

event_page_summary_v1.title: Event page summary
event_page_summary_v1.use: Name, date, location and format of an event, read from the event page URL column.

name.description: Name of the event as the page titles it.

date.description: Start date of the event, as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: End date of the event, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null for a single-day event.

location.description: Venue or city where the event takes place.

organizer.description: Company or group running the event.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on what the event is and who it is for.

registration_url.description: Link the page gives for registering or buying a ticket.

event_page_summary_v1.prompt: Read the event page and describe the event. Set name, date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD, plus location, organizer and registration_url from the page. Set format to in_person, virtual, hybrid or unknown. Write summary as two or three sentences on what the event is and who it is for. Set anything the page does not state to null.

filing_10k_locator_v1.title: 10-K filing link
filing_10k_locator_v1.use: Link to a public company's latest 10-K filing, searched from the company name or ticker column.

company.description: The public company's name or ticker.

filing_url.description: URL of the 10-K document itself, preferred over an index or listing page.

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year the filing covers, as a four-digit year.

filed_date.description: Date the filing was submitted, as YYYY-MM-DD.

filing_10k_locator_v1.prompt: Find the most recent 10-K annual report for {{company}} in the evidence. Put its document URL in filing_url, preferring the primary filing document over an index or listing page. Set fiscal_year to the year the report covers, filed_date to the filing date as YYYY-MM-DD, and document_format to html, pdf or unknown. Copy the URL exactly as the evidence gives it and never assemble one yourself. If the evidence identifies no 10-K, set the other fields to null and document_format to unknown.

filing_10k_initiatives_v1.title: 10-K strategic initiatives
filing_10k_initiatives_v1.use: Strategic initiatives named in an annual report, read from the filing URL column.

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year the filing covers, as a four-digit year.

initiatives.description: Each strategic initiative the filing describes.

description.description: One sentence on the initiative in the filing's own terms.

area.description: Part of the business the initiative belongs to.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on where the company is putting its effort.

filing_10k_initiatives_v1.prompt: Read the page and pull out the strategic initiatives management describes. Set company_name and fiscal_year from the document. Add one entry to initiatives for each, with a short name, a one-sentence description in the document's own terms, and area set to product, go_to_market, operations, financial or other. Write summary as two or three sentences on where the company is putting its effort. Use an empty list and null where the document does not say.

site_products_services_v1.title: Products and services
site_products_services_v1.use: What a company sells, read from the website URL column.

url.description: The company website or product page URL.

products.description: Each packaged product the page names.

services.description: Each delivered or ongoing service the page names.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the company sells.

site_products_services_v1.prompt: Read the page and list what this company sells. Put packaged products in products and delivered or ongoing work in services, one short name per entry. Write summary as one or two sentences on what the company sells overall. Use empty lists when the page names none.

site_blog_url_v1.title: Company blog URL
site_blog_url_v1.use: The URL of a company's own blog or news section, read from the homepage URL column.

blog_url.description: Absolute URL of the company's own blog or news section.

has_blog.description: True when the page links to such a section.

note.description: Short note on what the section is called when it is not called a blog.

site_blog_url_v1.prompt: Read the page and find the link to this company's own blog, news, insights or resources section. Put its absolute URL in blog_url and set has_blog to true. Ignore other companies' blogs, social profiles, and help or changelog pages, and use note when the section goes by another name. If the page has no such link, set has_blog to false and blog_url and note to null.

site_seo_keywords_v1.title: SEO keywords
site_seo_keywords_v1.use: Keywords a web page targets: its meta keywords, title and most frequent terms — deterministic, no model, read from the URL column.

site_target_industries_v1.title: Target industries
site_target_industries_v1.use: Industries a company sells into, read from the website URL column.

url.description: The company homepage or solutions page URL.

industries.description: Each industry the page says the company sells into.

evidence_note.description: Short qualifier, such as industries implied by customer logos only.

site_target_industries_v1.prompt: Read the page and list the industries this company sells into. Put one short industry name per entry in industries, keeping the page's own wording where it names them. Use evidence_note for a qualifier, such as when the industries are implied by customer logos rather than stated. If the page names no industries, use an empty list and set evidence_note to null.

site_icp_titles_v1.title: Buyer titles from website
site_icp_titles_v1.use: Buyer titles and personas a website speaks to, read from the website URL column.

url.description: The company homepage or product page URL.

titles.description: Each job title the page addresses or names as a buyer.

personas.description: Each broader buyer persona the page speaks to.

company_types.description: Each kind of company the page targets, such as size, stage or model.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the buyer this page speaks to.

site_icp_titles_v1.prompt: Read the page and work out who the company sells to. List the job titles it addresses in titles, broader buyer personas in personas, and the kinds of company it targets in company_types. Write summary as one or two sentences on the buyer this page speaks to. Use empty lists where the page does not say.

company_negative_feedback_v1.title: Negative customer feedback
company_negative_feedback_v1.use: Recurring complaints customers raise, searched from the company name column.

company.description: The company name.

themes.description: Each recurring complaint the evidence raises about the company.

frequency.description: How often the evidence repeats this complaint.

example.description: Short quote or paraphrase showing the complaint.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the overall pattern of complaints.

company_negative_feedback_v1.prompt: Find recurring complaints and criticisms of {{company}} in the evidence. Add one entry to themes for each, with a short theme, frequency set to frequent, occasional or rare based on how often the evidence repeats it, and a short example. Write summary as one or two sentences on the pattern. Use only the evidence; if it raises no complaints, use an empty list and say so in summary.

company_countries_v1.title: Countries of operation
company_countries_v1.use: Countries a company operates in, searched from the company name column.

company.description: The company name.

countries.description: Each country the company operates in, by its common English name.

headquarters_country.description: Country the headquarters sits in, or null when unstated.

company_countries_v1.prompt: Find the countries {{company}} operates in, using only the evidence. List each one in countries by its common English name, with no duplicates. Put the country of the headquarters in headquarters_country. If the evidence names no location, use an empty list and set headquarters_country to null.

linkedin_employee_count_v1.title: LinkedIn employee count
linkedin_employee_count_v1.use: Employee count read from a LinkedIn company payload already on the row — 0 credits.

payload.description: A column holding a LinkedIn company payload, e.g. from the company enrichment bundle or a LinkedIn company tool column.

industry_trends_v1.title: Industry trends
industry_trends_v1.use: Current trends shaping a market, searched from the industry column.

industry.description: The industry or market, e.g. 'B2B payments'.

trends.description: Each trend the evidence shows shaping the market.

direction.description: Which way the trend is moving.

evidence.description: One supporting detail, such as a figure or a named change.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on where the market is heading.

industry_trends_v1.prompt: Find the trends currently shaping {{industry}} in the evidence. Add one entry to trends for each, with a one-line trend statement, direction set to rising, falling, stable or unknown, and one supporting detail in evidence. Write summary as two or three sentences on where the market is heading. Use only the evidence, and an empty list when it shows no clear trend.

industry_demand_shocks_v1.title: Industry demand shocks
industry_demand_shocks_v1.use: Events that pushed demand up or down in a market, searched from the industry column.

industry.description: The industry or market, e.g. 'B2B payments'.

research.query_template: {{industry}} demand shock surge decline regulation news

shocks.description: Each event the evidence shows moving demand in the market.

direction.description: Which way the event moved demand.
